items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: And the decor was beautiful... hired John Kirby's band to play... So while we were playing there... Spencer had been to the doctor... I remember he lived over in Brooklyn, and we took him home to Brooklyn.

ctx.x: And Spencer, he had a very nice lady and he got married, so he made a complete about face. He wasn't going to drink anymore, he wasn't going to stay out late anymore, he wasn't going to gamble anymore, which worked in reverse. It backfired, you know, because he'd been used to -- he'd been living this life, you know, ever since he started in the business, I suppose. And it gave him a -- must have been some sort of a disease or something. It affected his mind. Because we were on the Apollo stage, like I started to…

do it, you know. It doesn't make any difference. But then I discovered something was wrong. So I walked over to him and I looked at him and I said, "Stop." I said, "This is the end. Stop." He said, "Now?" I said, "Yeah." And he stopped. Then the show was over and the fellow that used to work for Kirby, you know, drive the car and whatnot, he took him home. And that was the last I saw of him. And he died when I was in the army, in April of 1943 he died. No, '44. '44.
